title: RREP hop_count unbounded - input validation gap
description:
Location: rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs line 418

Issue: Unlike RREQ hop_limit which is clamped to MAX_HOP_LIMIT (15) at line 348 to prevent flood amplification, RREP hop_count is read verbatim without validation.

Security Impact: While RREP messages require signatures (preventing forgery), a misbehaving signed node could send RREP with hop_count=0 claiming to be 0 hops from destination. If routing logic prefers lower hop_count, attackers route gets selected.

Suggested Fix: Add validation consistent with RREQ: hop_count = data[1].min(MAX_HOP_LIMIT)
close_reason: Fixed — same root cause as project-LICHEN-worker6-595h (missing RX hop bound in the parse path), closed as dup-of-root-cause with one shared fix in rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs. Rrep::from_bytes now rejects hop_count > MAX_HOP_LIMIT(15) with LoadngError::HopLimitExceeded{got}. Deliberate divergence from the suggested .min(MAX_HOP_LIMIT) clamp: clamping admits the attacker packet with a rewritten metric (255 becomes a legal-looking 15), whereas rejection keeps it out of route selection entirely; this also matches the module's existing fail-closed convention (unknown ICMPv6 code, short buffer both rejected). Consistency check against canonical vectors: no compliant RREP exceeds 15 hops (rrep_max_hop_count=15 parses OK; rrep_zero_hop_count=0 parses OK) so rejection cannot drop legitimate traffic. New tests: rrep_hop_count_above_max_rejected (16 and 255), rrep_hop_count_boundaries_accepted. Verified: cargo test -p lichen-core --lib = 269 passed; module clippy-clean.
